newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon says 48 held in wave of arrests.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon says 48 held in wave of arrests.

text.p: Prosecutor-General Adnan Addoum said on Monday 48 people had been held in a wave of detentions of opposition figures in Lebanon in the past few days but 26 had already been freed.
None of the detainees had yet been charged with any offences, he told reporters at his office in response to questions.

Addoum's comments were the first time the government has said how many people have been held in sweeps by security forces since last Wednesday when a van carrying Syrian workers was machine-gunned in a predominantly Christian area, killing the driver and injuring some passengers.
Lebanese Christian opposition politicians at home and in Paris say 200 people have been detained but no independent confirmation of the figure was available.
Addoum's statement coincided with a call by France for Lebanon to respect democratic freedoms.
French Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux told reporters in Paris on Monday that France was convinced the Lebanese government would scrupulously abide by the rule of law.
"It is in no one's interest that this affair be used to restrict democratic freedoms in Lebanon," Dutriaux said.

He made the statement after Paris-based Lebanese Christians urged President Jacques Chirac to help put an end to the "persecution of peaceful Lebanese whose only crime is to want their country's freedom."
This was a reference to Christian nationalists who want Syria to withdraw from Lebanon the 35,000 troops which make it the main power broker in the country.

The Paris-based Rally for Lebanon (RPL), which is close to exiled anti-Syrian General Michel Aoun, said on Sunday the government was detaining and torturing hundreds of political opponents "instead of letting Lebanese justice do its work".
The RPL said detainees were accused of belonging to a pro-Israeli network in Lebanon, a charge carrying a possible death sentence.

Cardinal Nasrallah Sfeir, patriarch of Lebanon's Maronite church and the most powerful independent voice of the country's Christians, also questioned the legality of the detentions on Sunday, saying security forces were acting as "dawn visitors with no identity and no names".
"Citizens ask with anxiety and bitterness: Are there no legal principles of pursuit any more?" Sfeir said.

Addoum cited on Saturday increased activities against state security by "disruptive elements" aimed at disturbing Lebanon's relations with brotherly and friendly countries -- an apparent reference to Syria -- as the reason for the detentions.
He said specialised judicial authorities had authorised all branches of the security forces to investigate, hunt down and interrogate suspects.
